purpose: Category-level research for Power / Grid and adjacent data-centre electrical infrastructure.
categoryRead: Power / Grid remains the highest-quality structural Power Stack category, but the macro backdrop is less forgiving than the demand backdrop. Utility T&D, substations, switchgear, transformers and cable remain supported by data-centre and industrial load growth, while 10Y/30Y Treasury yields near 4.7%/5.25% raise valuation and financing risk for long-duration names. Prefer profitable equipment, engineering and regulated-grid exposures with backlog and pricing power over highly leveraged merchant-power or narrative-only names.

regionalRead.US: Demand remains strongest in grid equipment, transmission/substations, gas generation and data-centre balance-of-system. Long-end yields are again a valuation headwind after the initial Treasury-buyback relief faded.
regionalRead.HongKongChina: China kept the 1Y/5Y LPR at 3.00%/3.50%, signalling reliance on fiscal infrastructure execution rather than fresh monetary easing. This keeps the focus on state-backed power generation, grid and nuclear capex rather than a broad domestic-demand rebound.
regionalRead.Malaysia: The data-centre buildout continues to translate into real 275kV substation and high-voltage awards. The highest-quality local exposure remains businesses that can turn that demand into earnings without excessive customer concentration or working-capital stress.

newResearchCandidate.name: CBH Engineering Holding Berhad
newResearchCandidate.thesis: CBH is a direct Malaysian high-voltage substation and electrical-distribution exposure to hyperscale data-centre buildout. It is more differentiated than another general contractor because the work sits at the grid-connection layer and has already translated into a large order book and strong earnings growth.
newResearchCandidate.catalysts: Conversion of roughly RM600m of outstanding orders, further 275kV substation awards, a RM1.3bn tender pipeline and continued Johor/Selangor data-centre grid connections.
newResearchCandidate.risks: Heavy data-centre concentration, ACE Market liquidity/valuation risk, project execution, subcontractor dependence, working-capital swings and order-replenishment risk if hyperscaler capex slows.
newResearchCandidate.valuationTechnical: The stock had already risen materially before the latest award, so the quality bar is met but entry discipline matters. Prefer earnings and order-book confirmation over chasing contract headlines.
newResearchCandidate.evidence: On August 19 CBH disclosed a RM246m Johor data-centre contract involving high-voltage transformers and associated equipment for a 275kV substation. Q2 2026 net profit rose to RM24.53m from RM10.11m and revenue to RM120.93m from RM59.68m. Recent research estimates a RM1.3bn tender pipeline, mostly data-centre related.
